A_general.open_code_note: No source repository is available: the repository linked from npm (github.com/craft-io/craft-mcp-server) returned 404 in the v7 evidence collection. Craft publishes a separate local stdio server as npm package @craft-io/mcp-server (MIT, API key + CRAFT_API_URL) for the Public API; it is not the hosted OAuth server at mcp.craft.io and its tools are not added to actions.
A_general.license: MIT for the separate local npm package @craft-io/mcp-server; hosted server: N/A
other_official_servers: https://mcp-eu.craft.io/mcp — official EU-region endpoint; Craft says endpoint selection follows the account’s hosting region and a wrong-region connection fails.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Craft says there is no per-user MCP token cost and usage is subject to an account-level fair-use policy. MCP is available for Enterprise accounts and active trials; trials enable it automatically. Enterprise accounts require an admin to enable it.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Craft pricing lists Starter at $24/editor/month monthly or $19/editor/month annually, Pro at $99/editor/month monthly or $79/editor/month annually, and Enterprise at custom pricing. A 14-day Pro trial is offered.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Craft.io charges per Workspace Editor; the pricing FAQ describes unlimited viewers and contributors. MCP itself has no per-user token charge, but is subject to account-level fair use. MCP eligibility requires an Enterprise plan or active trial and an editor seat.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Enterprise MCP is disabled by default and requires admin enablement; trials enable it automatically. Contributor seats are excluded. Admins can set read-only access, narrow each user to selected workspaces, portfolios, and feedback portals, or block access. Requests are rate-limited; numeric limits were not found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Craft.io controls plan and service availability; account admins control organization and per-user MCP access, level, and scope; user permissions constrain accessible data.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Craft documents remote MCP access for reading, searching, creating, and updating product data. The official docs do not name individual tools; the Anthropic connector directory lists 31 tool names, but does not expose their schemas in the captured listing.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Craft says MCP responses can use markdown, flat/columnar output, and field-selected responses. Exact tool result schemas and error structures were not published in the evidence reviewed.

The reviewed official documentation does not specify MCP prompts exposed by the endpoint.
Craft says MCP actions are recorded in the affected item’s activity log, attributed to the connected user and marked “Via Agent.” The Account Manager MCP Users view also displays last-used time.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with a Bearer resource_metadata challenge. Protected-resource metadata names https://mcp.craft.io as authorization server, header bearer transport, and the listed scopes. Authorization-server metadata advertises authorization-code and refresh-token grants, PKCE S256, unauthenticated token endpoint clients, dynamic registration, and revocation. Craft docs say OAuth uses the user’s Craft sign-in; tokens last one hour and rotating refresh access can continue up to 90 days of inactivity. Token revocation endpoint is advertised; token lifetime is not otherwise specified by metadata.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthorized request returned JSON-RPC error code -32001 with message “Unauthorized: invalid or expired token” and id null.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; OAuth authorization code and refresh token grants; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth method none; Dynamic Client Registration endpoint https://mcp.craft.io/oauth/register; revocation endpoint https://mcp.craft.io/oauth/revoke; bearer token in header. Protected-resource scopes_supported: read:items:craft, write:items:craft, delete:items:craft, read:portfolios:craft, write:portfolios:craft, delete:portfolios:craft, read:feedback:craft, write:feedback:craft, manage:feedback-portal:craft, read:workspace-meta:craft, offline_access. Authorization-server scopes_supported lists only offline_access.

Craft says MCP errors are returned in a form the AI model can interpret, but the reviewed documentation does not give error schemas or describe a separate error-reporting capability.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Read, write, and destructive operations are implied by the listed tool names and Craft’s documentation of create/update/delete access. No tool annotations were found in the listing. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview-confirm flow was documented; user/client confirmation policy is Unknown. 3. OAuth identity is tied to a Craft user and inherits product permissions; admins can scope read-only/read-write access and block users or the organization. Enterprise MCP is off by default; trials enable it automatically. Token expiry is one hour; rotating refresh access can last up to 90 days of inactivity. 4. US and EU endpoints are documented; wrong-region access fails. Admin-configurable read-only mode and workspace/portfolio/feedback-portal scopes are documented. No toolset URL/header filters were found. 5. Craft says data access follows user permissions and admin scopes. AI-provider processing follows that provider’s terms and retention; Craft recommends reviewing them. No field-level masking rules were found. 6. Rate limits and account-level fair use are documented, without numeric values. No bulk caps, response caps, or per-call charges were found. 7. Parameter validation, coercion, aliases, and operator overrides are Unknown. 8. Actions are logged on affected items with user attribution and a Via Agent label; MCP Users shows last use. Request telemetry and opt-out were not found. 9. Feedback tools in the directory concern product/customer feedback management; no agent-rating or feedback-to-Craft reporting tool was identified. No MCP upsell responses were found. 10. Craft markets reusable workflow “skills”; no server instruction text or skill-delivery tool was documented. 11. Logs and last-used access metadata persist, but effects on later tool results or agent context are Unknown. 12. Separate US and EU regional endpoints are documented; no sub-server hierarchy was found. 13. No arbitrary API, SQL, script, or execution escape-hatch tool was identified in the available tool names.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Craft documents distinct US and EU hosted endpoints whose use depends on the account hosting region; a wrong-region connection fails.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official tool-name list was found in Craft’s documentation (https://help.craft.io/en/articles/15069070-introduction-to-the-craft-io-mcp-server). The Anthropic connector directory, identified as Craft-made and Anthropic-verified, names 31 tools; all 31 are listed in actions.json as third-party directory names. No tool schemas or parameter lists were available in the captured listing. APIs.io reports that tool names are not known; MartechDB also says the server requires sign-in before tool listing and does not name them. No additional catalogue-only names were added.
E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim initialize instructions and full tool definitions were available; the directory exposes names only.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Craft’s security documentation says MCP cannot add, remove, or change users; change account settings; or change billing or plan settings. Those operations remain available through Craft’s human/admin account surfaces. https://help.craft.io/en/articles/16960240-mcp-security-and-ai-data-handling

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Craft describes using MCP for feedback analysis, prioritization, PRD generation, roadmap updates, OKR planning, and executive updates. These are workflow claims/examples; the docs do not show server-enforced agent instructions or mandatory confirmation behavior.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Craft states: “MCP does not create any new access rights.” It says actions are recorded in the affected item’s activity log, user permissions apply, and admins can narrow scope. It also says the selected AI provider processes returned data under its own terms, retention policy, and data processing agreement.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Craft says MCP access is attributable to a real user, can be restricted by permissions and scope, and serves data from the organization’s hosting region. Its privacy policy says AI inputs are not used to train third-party AI models unless explicitly consented to; that policy describes AI features generally and does not specifically establish MCP-provider handling.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata and Craft’s access documentation support identity and scope enforcement; item activity logs and regional endpoint behavior are documented. Tool-level confirmation, input validation, field masking, and numeric rate limits were not evidenced. The privacy-policy AI-processing statements are general and cannot be confirmed as MCP-specific from the reviewed sources.

contradictions: Protected-resource metadata lists item, portfolio, feedback, and workspace-meta scopes, while authorization-server metadata lists only offline_access under scopes_supported.

Craft’s current authentication and security docs describe OAuth with standard Craft sign-in and say no API keys need to be created; an older Craft MCP article describes the implementation as using user-based API keys.
observations_for_research: Craft’s documented agent access is governed at both user-permission and administrator scope levels, with separate organization-wide and per-user controls.
The endpoint’s OAuth scopes expose read, write, and delete capability families even though Craft’s public documentation does not publish the individual MCP tool schemas.
Regional endpoint selection is tied to the data-hosting region, and Craft states that a wrong-region connection fails rather than routing to another region.
